title: Catching performance regressions in CI
question: The second question from a meeting with Cyrus: ^report(1) to ^report(5) found and fixed performance problems by hand, one profile at a time. What stops them coming back? What does Hazel's CI check today, why did its two benchmark workflows never work, why can a time not fail a build on GitHub's runners while a count can, what is the first count-based check (hazelgrove/hazel#2678), and should it build on #2161, an earlier benchmarking PR, or start fresh?

builds.name: dev's workflows
builds.note: the workflow files read; dev's branch protection and the runs' logs read with the GitHub CLI

builds.name: dev's CI runs
builds.note: the last ten green dev runs, 2026-09-22 to 10-09, each a different commit; the last five, with nearly the same tests (4,699-4,704), are the ones quoted
the first count-based check: Evaluator.evaluate_counting_work and the PerfBudgets test group, 'one small commit on today's dev'

builds.name: 2678, reuse off
builds.note: the same test, with reuse switched off in IncrEval.reuse_check, to see it fail

builds.name: the woods' picture view (update)
builds.note: the update, later on 2026-10-12: 'one build', with the variants compared in turn (the points strings made more directly; the view's call memo turned off)

runtime: CI times: GitHub's shared runners, as read from the runs' logs. Counts: node, on the laptop, in Hazel's quick test suite (#2678's PerfBudgets group, under a second). The update's view times: on the page, in a browser (the report does not name it).
runs: CI noise: the 'Test Successful in N s' lines of the last ten green dev runs (2026-09-22 to 10-09); the five most recent, with nearly the same suite (4,699-4,704 tests), are the ones quoted. Counts: #2678's test run twice, and once with reuse switched off; 'the counts are the same on every run'. Update: one build, the variants compared in turn; changes in the whole redraw 'were too noisy to see', so the view's own evaluation was timed.

measures.Time (What CI runs today): min or h: each workflow's run time, from its runs' logs read with the GitHub CLI (the report does not say how many runs each)
measures.full test job: s: the full test job's 'Test Successful in N s' time over the last five dev runs: 1,110-1,453 s, mean 1,323 s, standard deviation 127 s (about 10%)
measures.quick job: s: the quick job's time over the same five runs: 145-147 s four times, 87 s once
measures.Steps now: count: the steps the evaluator's trampoline actually took (Evaluator.evaluate_counting_work); a result taken from the cache counts as the one step that fetches it. Not the evaluator's older step count, which counts a reused subtree's steps again
measures.Budget: count: the PerfBudgets test's ceiling per case; the re-run must also stay under 5% of a cold run, whatever the budgets
measures.Steps (update): count: evaluation steps of the woods' picture view
measures.The view's time (update): ms: the view's own evaluation on the page, a timer around it

times: CI: the logs' 'Test Successful in N s' lines. The update: a timer around the view's own evaluation, the variants compared in turn on one build.

PerfBudgets, cold run.program: recursion, list traversals and case matches (a smaller bench/eval-bench.hz)

PerfBudgets, re-run with reuse switched.result: fails: 'over its budget of 420. A performance regression'

cited.what: the last two real successes of /perf, on #2161; one on 08-12 'succeeded' with nothing to compare against; the last run on dev, 09-30, exited with 'No such file or directory'
the threshold at which #2161's comparison script marks a change (it always exits successfully)
cited.from: the benchmark workflows' comparison script, from #2161

cited.what: #2161, 'Performance benchmarking', by David Moon: a draft opened 2026-03-05, last commit 2026-03-13

cited.number: median of 10 runs; let-chains of 100 and 500 bindings
cited.what: #2161's harness, bench/hazel_bench.re, timing the editor's syntax and statics phases in four scenarios
the cost of a run of #2161's separate job, building base and head
the woods' picture, rebuilt whole in one step at every typed parameter it crossed, by giving a value a type
the view, after removing that copying, with its step count not much changed

provenance: No raw file was kept with this report: the CI logs were read with the GitHub CLI and not saved, the counts are as #2678's test printed them, and the update's times exist only as printed (the table under #update). Every number here exists only as printed in the report.
